assumptions.choice: The initialization and post-assignment core entries use plain self.buy().
assumptions.reason: The specification gives examples but no exact quantity; canonical defaults require plain entries when sizing is unstated.

assumptions.choice: A tranche is 20% of the current position, raised to 100 shares when at least 100 shares are available, and capped by the remaining core-position capacity.
assumptions.reason: This implements the stated 20% tranche, minimum 100-share rule, and maximum 100% total-sale constraint.

assumptions.choice: Each completed tranche maintains its own virtual strike and expiry bar.
assumptions.reason: Additional tranches can be added during rolling, so independent tranche state is needed to apply each stated seven-bar term.

assumptions.choice: If a tranche reaches its seventh bar without the price remaining above the upper band, it stays active until the stated mean-reversion buyback condition occurs.
assumptions.reason: The specification defines a roll only when price remains above the upper band and defines buyback only for the stated middle-band or RSI conditions.

assumptions.choice: Forced assignment is evaluated against the current upper Bollinger band plus the current ATR.
assumptions.reason: The condition says upper band plus one ATR and does not specify use of the recorded virtual strike.
